Gorakhpur
(‘city of गोरख्नाथ्’)
------------------------------------------
Situated on the bank of the river Rāpti, at a distance of 240 kms. (150 miles) to the north of वाराणसी or काशी in Uttar Pradesh, this city is the Head-quarters of the नाथ चुल्त्. A beautiful temple built over the समाधि (place of बुरिअल्) of the well-known sage गोरख्नाथ् (also spelt as Gorakha/Gorakṣa-nātha) who perhaps lived in the eleventh century A. D., is the main religious attraction of this place. The sanctum houses the समाधि. Behind it is an image of मोथेर् Kālī. An oil lamp is kept burning always near the image and never allowed to be put out.
The मठ (monastery) is a part of the temple campus. Its head (called ‘mahanta’) is considered as a perfect being.
One of the chief attractions of this place is the गीता प्रेस्स् which is doing commendable service in spreading Hindu religion and culture. (See GĪTĀ PRESS.)
The town now has a University and is also a centre of trade, industry and commerce.

Gorakhnāth
------------------------------------------
The नाथ चुल्त्, with its stress on हठयोग and a philosophy of advaita preceded the भक्ति Movement. The cult recognises 84 teachers (known as सिद्धस्) out of which 9 are considered more important. The founder was आदिनाथ who was an इन्चर्नतिओन् of Lord शिव. मत्स्येन्द्रनाथ was his disciple. Gorakhanāth (or Gorakṣanātha) was his chief disciple and successor.
Very little is known of his life or activities. According to the traditions of the cult he was ‘born’ out of a cow-dung heap as a twelve-year old boy and joined his गुरु मत्स्येन्द्रनाथ. According to some scholars, he belonged to the Northern Karnataka region and might have flourished during the eleventh century A. D.
Many stories are current in the annals of the नाथ चुल्त् about his miraculous powers and yogic attainments.
The Vīraśaiva tradition of Karnataka narrates an incident according to which Gorakhanāth was vanquished by अल्लम प्रभु in a test of Haṭhayogic powers and became his disciple!
Several works on various aspects of योग, both in Sanskrit and in Hindi, are attributed to him. Some of them are:
SANSKRIT:Amanaska, Amaraugha-śāsana,
Gorakṣapaddhati, Gorakṣaśataka,
Gorakṣasaṁhitā,
Siddha-सिद्धान्त-paddhati. HINDI:Sabadī, Gyāncautīsā, Gyāntilak,
Machindra-gorakh-bodh. There is reason to believe that there was a great tradition of esoteric योग practices even before the time of Gorakh-nāth which was common to the Hindus and the Buddhists. He might have gathered material from both while composing his works.
His philosophy is akin to शैविस्म् and Advaita Vedānta. गुरु and monastic disciplines have been given a place of supreme importance.
See also MATSYENDRANĀTHA and the NĀTHA-CULT.
